title: Raw Numeric Offset Bit-Flag Comments
pattern: Inline comments detailing bitwise offsets and boolean flags directly in raw numeric operations.
why_bad: High error rate. Developers cannot easily query, inspect, or modify raw offsets safely. Updating bitfields requires editing prose and code in parallel.
detection: Comments explaining raw numeric offsets or shifts on integers used as status containers.
counterexample: A declarative `bitflags!` definition naming each bit as a compiler-checked constant (`const PRINTER_READY = 1 << 4;`).
fix: Use a declarative bitfield macro (like `bitflags!`) to make each flag a named compiler constant, removing the offset comment.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Stamp comments related to a variable with the variable's name").
